chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who threw [a stone] at game, broke his hand or leg, and left it, so the game grazed [or remained]. He said: 'Upon him is one-quarter of the redemption money.'

key_terms.فِدَاءٌ: Redemption money or compensation for breaking Ihram rules

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for accidentally breaking a limb while hunting in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim clarifies the specific penalty for accidental self-injury during the act of hunting while in Ihram, establishing a quarter of the standard fidyah as the compensation. It highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the liability for the game itself and the incidental harm to the hunter, reflecting the detailed legal methodology of the Ahl al-Bayt. The ruling underscores the principle that minor, unintentional physical impediments incurred during the ritual act do not invalidate the Ihram but require proportional expiation.
